title: First Aid Paper 4: Bandaging, CPR and Ward Care
source: Adapted from user-provided First Aid and Nursing question banks

objective.question: The following are uses of bandages, except:
objective.explanation: Bandages do not themselves prevent infection.

objective.question: Which of the following is not a sign of successful CPR?
objective.explanation: Fixed over-dilated pupils are not success.

objective.question: When a dressing becomes saturated with blood, the first aider should:
options: Remove it and apply new dressing
Leave it and apply additional dressing on top
objective.explanation: Add dressing on top; do not remove.

objective.question: A type of open wound with jagged skin edges and free bleeding is known as:
A first aider should avoid moving an injured victim until all injuries are identified so:
options: Victim will not suffer unnecessary pain
Victim will not suffer further injury

objective.question: The primary survey is conducted in the order of check for:
objective.explanation: Breathing, then pulse and bleeding in this set.

objective.question: The immediate first aid action for arterial bleeding on the right hand is to:
options: Apply digital pressure over the bleeding site
objective.explanation: Apply digital pressure over the site.

objective.question: Which position is appropriate for nursing an unconscious patient?
The first aid action for an impaled arrow through the chest is:
options: Remove the arrow and apply gauze
Pad and bandage around the arrow, do not remove
Break the back part and bandage

structured.question: Differentiate between shock and fainting. (4 marks)
markingGuide: Definition and causes of each: 2 marks.
Differences in onset and management: 2 marks.
structured.modelAnswer: Shock is circulatory failure; fainting is brief loss from reduced brain blood.

structured.question: State the difference between burns and scalds. (4 marks)
structured.modelAnswer: Burns are from dry heat; scalds from wet heat.

structured.question: Outline four roles of a nurse in medical care. (4 marks)
markingGuide: Four roles such as caregiver and educator: 4 marks.

structured.question: Write the difference between compound and simple fracture. (4 marks)
structured.modelAnswer: Simple is closed; compound breaks the skin.

structured.question: As a first aider, state the management for a simple fracture of the right arm. (4 marks)
structured.modelAnswer: Support, immobilise with splint/sling, monitor and refer.
